To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IT governance is shaped by the investment characteristics, the external environment, and the internal context, and that these factors are more important to understand than the allocation of decision rights in shaping IT governance.
IT governance patterns are shaped by IT investment characteristics and organizational contextual factors.
IT governance archetypes vary depending on investment characteristics, external environment, and internal organizational factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how IT governance is shaped by the characteristics of IT investments, the external environment, and the internal context of the organization.
IT governance in IT investment decision processes and how it is affected by contextual factors.
IT governance and its relationship to the initiation, development, and approval stages of IT investment decision processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IT governance archetypes identified and described in this study are the result of a complex interplay between the characteristics of the IT investments, the organizations' external environment, and their internal context.
IT governance archetypes vary with IT investment characteristics, external environment, and internal organization, and these factors should be considered in the governance of IT investment processes.

the IT investment decision processes of the six hospitals in our sample can be characterized by a set of IT governance archi-types that vary with the level of investment, external influence, centralization of organization, and power of the IT function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IT governance is not a static concept.
the IT department may have little influence in the IT investment process, especially when the investment is small and there are no external influences.
IT governance is not a one-dimensional construct.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IT governance literature needs to be broadened to encompass the entire IT investment decision process, including its initiation and development stages, to provide a more complete view of the IT investment decision-making process.
IT governance is more complex than previously assumed, and the allocation of final approval rights is only one aspect.

organizations should consider IT governance as an ongoing process that involves multiple participants and that the allocation of IT governance rights should be considered in conjunction with other contextual factors.
